title: Lifting prescribed isolated local deformations of an affine scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjective homomorphism of finite-dimensional commutative $k$-algebras, each with an augmentation to $k$ whose kernel is its unique maximal ideal, and suppose the homomorphism respects the augmentations. Let $V$ be an affine finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ be distinct closed points such that $V$ is smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] away from them. Let $Y$ be an affine scheme flat over $A$ [def-weil-flat-morphism] with a specified isomorphism $Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}k\cong V$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use this nilpotent special fibre to identify the points of $Y$ with those of $V$. For each $i$, let $D_i$ be a local $A'$-algebra (a ring with a unique maximal ideal), flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], with a specified isomorphism $\delta_i:D_i\otimes_{A'}A\cong\mathcal O_{Y,p_i}$. Here tensor products have their usual algebra structure [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then there are an affine scheme $Y'$ flat over $A'$, an isomorphism $\alpha:Y'\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A'}\operatorname{Spec}A\cong Y$, and local $A'$-algebra isomorphisms $\beta_i:\mathcal O_{Y',p_i}\cong D_i$. The reduction of $\beta_i$ followed by $\delta_i$ equals the local-ring identification $\mathcal O_{Y',p_i}\otimes_{A'}A\cong\mathcal O_{Y,p_i}$ induced by $\alpha$. The case $r=0$ is included.

source.place: Tag 0DZF, lemma-isolated, first smooth arrow, unpacked using Tag 0DYX, lemma-affine, and Example example-rings; smoothness includes a compatible isomorphism over the given deformation. Only the first arrow is asserted; no henselization, completion or tangent-space clause.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian] the base rings are Artinian; [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent] makes them Noetherian with nilpotent maximal ideals. The kernel $J=\ker(A'\to A)$ lies in the maximal ideal of $A'$, hence is nilpotent. In any algebra over one of these bases, its maximal-ideal extension is nilpotent, so every prime contains it; inverse image and quotient therefore give mutually inverse bijections of prime ideals with the special fibre. This also identifies the unique prime above any specified special-fibre point. These observations justify all point labels and all inverse-image multiplicative subsets used below. Explicitly, for a multiplicative subset $S\subset P$, use its full inverse image under each reduction map to $P$; at $p_i$ this is the complement of the unique prime over $\mathfrak m_i$. Thus the localization maps in steps 4–6 refer to the same marked local lifting problem at every stage.

source.place: Tag 0DZF, lemma-isolated: Artinian coefficient rings and nilpotent special fibres

proof.text: Write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]. Apply [lem-sbc-finite-affine-tensor-base-change] for a single affine summand: the given special-fibre marking identifies $P=B\otimes_Ak$ with $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$. By [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra], $P$ is finite type over $k$. The nilpotent lifting lemma [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-lift-nilpotent] implies that $B$ is finite type over $A$, and the affine flatness criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] makes it a flat $A$-algebra. Let $\mathfrak m_i\subset P$ be the maximal ideals of the closed points $p_i$, and let $\mathfrak q_i\subset B$ be their inverse images. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $\mathcal O_{Y,p_i}=B_{\mathfrak q_i}$. Thus $\delta_i$ marks the reduction of $D_i$ as that localization.

source.place: Tags 0DYX, lemma-affine, and 0DZF, lemma-isolated, passage to flat algebra deformations

proof.text: Filter $J$ using [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-ideal-length-one-filtration], say $0=J_0\subset\cdots\subset J_s=J$, and put $C_t=A'/J_{s-t}$ for $0\leq t\leq s$. Then $C_0=A$, $C_s=A'$, and $C_{t+1}\to C_t$ has length-one kernel $I_t$. This kernel is annihilated by the maximal ideal: multiplication by that ideal sends a simple module either to zero or to itself, and the latter is impossible because the ideal is nilpotent. Each kernel lies in the maximal ideal of its augmented source, so $I_t^2=0$. Hence these are small extensions. Put $D_{i,t}=D_i\otimes_{A'}C_t$. They are flat over $C_t$: on any injection of $C_t$-modules, tensoring with $D_{i,t}$ is the same as tensoring the underlying injection over $A'$ with $D_i$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Tensor associativity identifies successive reductions, and reduction modulo a nilpotent ideal of the local ring $D_i$ is local. We inductively construct flat finite-type $C_t$-algebras $B_t$, starting with $B_0=B$, reduction isomorphisms $a_t:B_{t+1}\otimes_{C_{t+1}}C_t\cong B_t$, and local isomorphisms $b_{i,t}:(B_t)_{p_i}\cong D_{i,t}$. At $t=0$ use $b_{i,0}=\delta_i^{-1}$. Require for each $t$ that $\rho_{i,t}(b_{i,t+1}\otimes C_t)=b_{i,t}(a_t)_{p_i}$, where $\rho_{i,t}:D_{i,t+1}\otimes C_t\cong D_{i,t}$ is the tensor-associativity map.

source.place: Tag 0DZF, first smooth arrow: reduction to small extensions, with the marked induction stated explicitly

proof.text: Fix $t$ and the inductive data. The special fibre of $B_t$ is still $P$. Set $N_t=P\otimes_kI_t$, a finite $P$-module, and $T^j=\operatorname{Ext}^j_P(L_{P/k},N_t)$ for $j=1,2$. By [lem-sfb-cotangent-ext-smooth-support], both are finite $P$-modules, their localizations are the corresponding local cotangent Ext groups, and they vanish at every prime where $V/k$ is smooth. Their supports therefore lie in $\{\mathfrak m_1,\ldots,\mathfrak m_r\}$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-maximal-support-localization] to obtain isomorphisms $T^j\cong\prod_i(T^j)_{\mathfrak m_i}$. Its Noetherian hypothesis follows from [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] applied to $k\to P$; a field is Noetherian because its only ideals are zero and the whole field.

source.place: Tag 0DZF, first arrow: finite support of positive cotangent cohomology, as in lemma-first-order-localization

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-flat-algebra-small-extension-control], the obstruction to a marked flat lift of $B_t$ to $C_{t+1}$ is an element $o\in T^2$. For each $i$, the prescribed $D_{i,t+1}$ is a marked flat lift of $(B_t)_{p_i}$: its reduction marking is $b_{i,t}^{-1}\rho_{i,t}$. Naturality of that obstruction, composed with the localization isomorphism $(T^2)_{\mathfrak m_i}\cong T^2(P_{\mathfrak m_i},(N_t)_{\mathfrak m_i})$ of [lem-sfb-cotangent-ext-smooth-support], identifies its local obstruction with $o_{\mathfrak m_i}$, and existence of this marked local lift makes it zero. Injectivity of the product map in the preceding step forces $o=0$. Choose a marked flat lift $(B^*,a)$ of $B_t$. It is finite type over $C_{t+1}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-lift-nilpotent], applied to the square-zero ideal $I_t$. By [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness], its localizations are flat over $C_{t+1}$.

source.place: Tag 0DZF, first arrow: local obstruction vanishing gives a global lift

proof.text: Let $x_i$ be the marked class of $(B^*)_{p_i}$ and $y_i$ that of $D_{i,t+1}$, both marked over $(B_t)_{p_i}$ as above. The torsor assertion of [lem-sfb-flat-algebra-small-extension-control] gives a unique $u_i\in(T^1)_{\mathfrak m_i}$, the local torsor group being identified with $(T^1)_{\mathfrak m_i}$ by the localization isomorphism of [lem-sfb-cotangent-ext-smooth-support], with $x_i+u_i=y_i$. Surjectivity of $T^1\to\prod_i(T^1)_{\mathfrak m_i}$ from [lem-sfb-finite-maximal-support-localization] gives $u$ with these coordinates. Replace $(B^*,a)$ by a marked lift in its torsor class $x+u$. Localization preserves the torsor action by [lem-sfb-flat-algebra-small-extension-control], so each local class now equals $y_i$. Choose the resulting marked isomorphisms as $b_{i,t+1}$ and call the new algebra $B_{t+1}$, with marking $a_t$. Equality as marked classes means precisely $b_{i,t}^{-1}\rho_{i,t}(b_{i,t+1}\otimes C_t)=(a_t)_{p_i}$; multiplying by $b_{i,t}$ proves the induction equation, including the reduction compatibility. Nilpotent lifting of finite type again applies to this representative. When $r=0$, the two support modules are zero; the same argument supplies a lift and there are no adjustment conditions.

source.place: Tag 0DZF, first arrow: adjust the global lift to realize the specified local lifts with their markings

proof.text: Induction yields $B_s$ over $A'$ and the composite reduction marking $a:B_s\otimes_{A'}A\cong B$. Compose the induction equations of step 3; at $t=0$ one has $b_{i,0}=\delta_i^{-1}$, so they give $\delta_i(b_{i,s}\otimes_{A'}A)=a_{p_i}$. Set $Y'=\operatorname{Spec}B_s$. The one-summand affine base-change formula [lem-sbc-finite-affine-tensor-base-change] makes $a$ into $\alpha:Y'\times_{A'}A\cong Y$, and each stalk is flat over $A'$ by [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness]. The spectrum of $A'$ has one point with local ring $A'$, so [def-weil-flat-morphism] gives flatness of $Y'$ over $A'$. The stalk dictionary [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies $b_{i,s}$ with $\beta_i:\mathcal O_{Y',p_i}\cong D_i$. These ring isomorphisms are local because both rings are local. Under the same dictionary the displayed equation is exactly the required compatibility with $\alpha$. Thus all clauses, including $J=0$, empty $V$, and $r=0$, hold.
